'''Tom Braunlich''' is an American customizable card game designer credited as a designer of Decipher's ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game (SWCCG).<ref name="wp-swccg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia (designer credit line)</ref><ref name="wp-braunlich">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Braunlich Tom Braunlich], Wikipedia</ref>

== SWCCG role ==

Wikipedia lists Braunlich among SWCCG's designers, together with [[Rollie Tesh]], [[Warren Holland]], and [[Jerry Darcy]].<ref name="wp-swccg" /> Wikipedia's Braunlich article states that he worked for [[Decipher|Decipher, Inc.]] and helped create SWCCG, calling it Decipher's most monetarily successful CCG and second-most successful game by longevity.<ref name="wp-braunlich" />

A 2022 Booster Pack interview presents Braunlich (with design partner Tesh) as designers of Decipher's ''Star Trek'' and ''Star Wars'' CCGs, discussing moving from ''Star Trek'' design into ''Star Wars'' and aiming for a cinematic feel in the rules.<ref name="booster">[https://theboosterpack.buzzsprout.com/1692574/episodes/10935581-booster-pack-throwback-28-decipher-s-star-wars-ccg-with-designer-tom-braunlich Booster Pack Throwback &mdash; Decipher's Star Wars CCG with designer Tom Braunlich], 2022</ref>

== Path into Decipher CCGs ==

Braunlich is from Tulsa, Oklahoma, and is a journalism graduate.<ref name="wp-braunlich" /> With Rollie Tesh he was a world champion of ''Pente'' (later published by Decipher).<ref name="wp-braunlich" /><ref name="wp-decipher">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decipher,_Inc. Decipher, Inc.], Wikipedia</ref> In 1993 Braunlich and Tesh approached Decipher with an idea for a licensed collectible card game; the result was ''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' CCG (1994).<ref name="wp-braunlich" /><ref name="wp-decipher" /><ref name="st-timeline">[https://web.archive.org/web/20080821113824/http://decipher.com/content/2004/st10/sttimeline.html The History of Star Trek CCG: The Timeline], Kathy McCracken, Decipher (Wayback)</ref> Virginian-Pilot coverage of the December 1995 ''Star Wars'' launch is cited on Wikipedia's Braunlich page.<ref name="wp-braunlich" />

Former Decipher staffer [[Mark Tuttle]] later described SWCCG as "Tom and Rollie's &hellip; game," recalling Braunlich recruiting him from ''Star Trek'' CCG community work into ''Star Wars'' playtesting.<ref name="fantha">[https://www.fanthatracks.com/interviews/guest-interview-mark-tuttle/ Guest Interview: Mark Tuttle], Fantha Tracks, 15 March 2018</ref> The GeoCities anagram table unscrambles [[Nabrun Leids]] as Braunlich (printed with a question mark as "Decipherian?" on the fan page; Encyclopedia 3.2 labels it game creator).<ref name="ana">[https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/anagrams.html Anagramed Decipherians]</ref>

== Other activity (brief) ==

Wikipedia summarizes additional work as a games writer (including ''Pente'' and chess) and chess tournament organizer, and notes a USCF Life Master chess rating.<ref name="wp-braunlich" />
